info.title: freehire API — original job links and catalogue export
info.description:
## Base URL

All endpoints are served under `https://freehire.me/api/v1`. The API is read-first and open: the job, search, facet, and company endpoints need no authentication and may be called cross-origin.

Authenticated endpoints accept either the browser session cookie (set by sign-in, same-origin) or a personal API key sent as a Bearer token — see the authentication model below. Keys are created in your account, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys), not through this API.

## Response envelope

Single items are wrapped as `{ "data": ... }`. Collections add pagination metadata: `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "total", "limit", "offset" } }`. Errors are `{ "error": "message" }` with a matching HTTP status.

```json
{ "data": { "...": "single item" } }

{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total": 4213, "limit": 20, "offset": 0 } }

{ "error": "job not found" }
```

## Pagination

List and search endpoints page with `limit` (default 20, max 100) and `offset` (default 0). `meta.total` reports the total matching the current filters, so you can compute the number of pages.

Pagination is bounded on **every** list endpoint: `offset + limit` may not exceed 10000 (`pagination too deep` → 400). This is deep-paging protection, not a cap on the reported total — use filters to narrow rather than paging that far.

The bound is a refusal rather than a clamp, deliberately: a clamped page would answer 200 carrying rows you did not ask for, and a client walking pages would loop over the same page forever without being able to tell. A 400 means "there is no such page", which is the truth.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes: 400 (bad request / invalid value), 401 (missing or invalid credentials), 403 (authenticated but not allowed, e.g. a non-moderator), 404 (no such job, company, or owned resource), 429 (request limit exceeded), and 503 (service temporarily unavailable). Application errors use `{ "error": ... }`. nginx rate-limit rejections can return a non-JSON body; see API plans below.

## API plans

The public read endpoints answer without a key for personal and non-commercial use. Showing the postings in a product you offer to others needs an [API plan](https://freehire.me/jobs-api), under the [data licence](https://freehire.me/terms#data-licence).

Send a full-access key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or use the OAuth access token of a signed-in MCP or CLI connection.

The API plan allows 1,200 requests per 60-second window. On the original-link endpoints (`/data/jobs/search`, `/data/jobs/{slug}`) each plan is counted apart: 1,200 for the API plan, 6,000 for the Data plan, which holds the API plan's 1,200 everywhere else. Neither paid API plan has a daily request cap.

Job reads do not carry the employer's own links: `url` is empty and `source_url` absent wherever `apply_url`, the freehire redirect to the same page, is set. The `/data/jobs` endpoints serve both to either paid API plan. The account shares one budget across its full-access API keys and OAuth connections, including public REST reads and agent search. A browser session cookie does not select the paid API rate.

The limit counts HTTP requests, not returned listings or unique vacancies. A page containing 100 listings costs one request. Re-fetching the same page or vacancy costs another request, including when the data has not changed. There is no separate cooldown for refreshing a vacancy.

Pagination returns 20 listings by default and up to 100 with `limit=100`. Requests carrying `offset` or `company_slug` also pass through separate per-IP nginx limits of 2 requests per second each, including paid requests. The `offset` limit allows a burst of 50 excess requests; the `company_slug` limit allows 30. A request carrying both parameters draws on both limits. For sustained pagination or company-filtered reads, keep the combined traffic from one IP within the applicable 2-request-per-second limit.

The gateway returns `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until reset). A window starts with its first request. Exceeding a request limit returns HTTP 429. Gateway rejections include `Retry-After` in seconds; nginx rejections can omit these headers and return a non-JSON body. Pause for `Retry-After` when present; otherwise back off before retrying.

## Data freshness and closed jobs

A posting is **open** until something closes it, and a closed posting carries `closed_at` and a `closed_reason`. Nothing is deleted. These are the closers, with the `closed_reason` each writes:

- The crawl no longer lists the posting: `unseen`. A crawl that ran incompletely, or whose board failed, closes nothing.
- A source that streams removals reports the posting taken down: `feed_removed`.
- Two consecutive liveness reads find the page expired, or the source answers that it is gone: `probe_expired`.
- A source with no close signal at all is closed by age (`expired`), and so is a posting whose application deadline has passed. The age rule is a guess, which is why the reason says so.
- A board whose crawl has failed for a long time (`board_unreachable`, `board_gone`) or has listed nothing for a long time (`feed_empty`), or a board that was retired (`board_retired`).
- An aggregator's copy of a posting whose employer's own board freehire already crawls closes in favour of that copy (`ats_covered`).
- A moderator (`moderated`), or the employer on a posting they published themselves (`employer_closed`).
- The employer deleting a posting they published themselves (`employer_deleted`). Unlike every other closer this is final: the posting leaves every list and `GET /jobs/{slug}` answers 404. The row is kept for the applications that reference it.

Postings closed before the reason was recorded carry an empty `closed_reason`. A closed posting can **reopen**: when its source lists it again, or a moderator reopens it, `closed_at` is cleared.

How often a posting is re-checked is set by each source's crawl schedule, and it differs by source; this API does not promise a figure. Search also withholds an open posting its source has not shown for 14 days, but only for sources where a missing listing is evidence: some sources have a longer window of their own, and self-closing, liveness-probed and manually added sources are excluded. An old `last_seen_at` alone does not prove a posting is out of search. Such a posting stays open and `GET /jobs/{slug}` serves it.

Closed postings never appear in `GET /jobs`, in search or in a company's open postings. `GET /jobs/{slug}` keeps serving them, with `closed_at` set, so a link you stored still resolves. A company's recent closed postings are at `GET /companies/{slug}/closed-jobs`. Interview prep also serves a closed public posting when the caller has a signed-in session and an application at the interview stage.

### Finding companies by domain

If you hold a list of company web domains, `GET /companies/by-domain?domain=stripe.com&domain=https://www.acme.io/careers` (repeatable or comma-joined, up to 100) returns `{"data": [{"domain", "slug", "name", "job_count", "website"}], "meta": {"unmatched": [...]}}`. Domains are compared by host (lowercase, no `www.`, port or trailing dot) against each company's site; every match is returned, including companies with `job_count` 0, and domains with no match are listed in `meta.unmatched`. Then read a company's postings with `GET /jobs/search?company_slug=<slug>` (repeatable), or subscribe a change webhook with `company_slugs` to have only their changes pushed.

### Keeping a mirror in sync

`GET /jobs/changes` is the feed of every opening, closing and reopening of a public, canonical posting. To keep a copy of the catalogue current:

1. Load the postings you want through the list and search endpoints, and note the time you started.
2. Call `GET /jobs/changes?since=<that time>` and follow `meta.next_cursor` as `cursor` until `meta.has_more` is false. Store the last `next_cursor`.
3. From then on, call `GET /jobs/changes?cursor=<stored cursor>` on your own schedule. A `closed` change means delist the posting; `opened` and `reopened` mean fetch it with `GET /jobs/{slug}` and list it.

The cursor is a position, not a time, so a walk never skips or repeats a change while new ones arrive. Each change carries a `seq`: for a given `public_slug`, apply a change only when its `seq` is greater than the last one you applied, and skip it otherwise. The feed can serve one posting's changes slightly out of order, and the first call with `since` can repeat a few changes from just before it; this rule makes both harmless. `since` can reach back 30 days at most, and the feed begins when it was introduced (`meta.available_since`). A change shows up in the feed shortly after it happens, not at the same instant: the feed trails the oldest transaction still open in the database, so a long-running one delays new entries until it ends. Nothing is lost, only late.

The feed keeps the full history and nothing is deleted from it, so a `cursor` you hold never expires. Only `since` is capped, at 30 days back, so a first call stays cheap: a mirror older than that rebuilds from search and then starts the feed with `since`.

A posting counts as listed while it is open, canonical (not a duplicate of another posting) and public. A posting that stops being listed is a `closed` change whose `closed_reason` is the close reason, or `duplicate` when it became a duplicate of another posting, or `private`; one that is listed again is `reopened`.

### Change webhooks

Instead of polling the feed you can have it pushed. `POST /me/change-webhooks` subscribes a URL (with an `api` or `api_data` plan); the answer carries the signing `secret`, **once**. A subscription can ask for only some companies (`company_slugs`) and some kinds of change (`kinds`), and receives changes made from about the time it was created (a change from the moment just before can arrive once; `seq` dedupes it). It reads the same feed as `GET /jobs/changes`, in the same order, and the same postings.

A delivery is a `POST` with a JSON body and these headers:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-Freehire-Timestamp` | Unix seconds when it was signed. |
| `X-Freehire-Signature` | `v1=` plus the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by your secret, of the timestamp, a `.`, and the raw body. |
| `X-Freehire-Delivery` | An id, the same for a retry of the same batch. |
| `X-Freehire-Event` | `job.changes`, or `webhook.test` for a test. |

```json
{"id": "7-4821-90210", "type": "job.changes", "changes": [
  {"public_slug": "senior-go-engineer-acme-1a2b", "company_slug": "acme", "seq": 98765, "kind": "closed", "at": "2026-06-20T04:10:00Z", "closed_reason": "unseen"}
]}
```

`changes` is a batch of up to 100, oldest first, each shaped like a feed change plus `company_slug`. Apply a change only when its `seq` is greater than the last one you applied for that `public_slug` (this also drops a repeat). `opened` and `reopened` mean fetch the posting with `GET /jobs/{slug}`; `closed` means delist it.

Verify before you trust a body: recompute the HMAC over the timestamp header, `.` and the **raw** body bytes (not re-serialised JSON), compare in constant time, and refuse a timestamp more than 5 minutes from your clock. In Go:

```go
func verify(secret, ts, sig string, body []byte) bool {
	n, err := strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
	if err != nil || math.Abs(time.Since(time.Unix(n, 0)).Seconds()) > 300 {
		return false
	}
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
	fmt.Fprintf(mac, "%s.", ts)
	mac.Write(body)
	return hmac.Equal([]byte("v1="+hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))), []byte(sig))
}
```

Answer any `2xx` to accept a batch. Anything else, a timeout (10 seconds) or a redirect counts as a failure: the same batch is sent again after 30 seconds, doubling up to an hour. Delivery is at least once, so expect repeats and dedupe on `seq`. After 25 failures in a row, or at once on a `410 Gone`, the subscription is disabled (`disabled_at` and `disabled_reason` in the list); delete it and create it again to resume, from the changes made then. Plan for the feed instead if you need what happened meanwhile. While your plan has lapsed, deliveries pause and pick up where they stopped once it is renewed.

## Authentication model

Browser clients authenticate with an `HttpOnly` session cookie set on sign-in (same-origin; the SPA cannot read it). Non-browser clients use a personal API key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Endpoints marked “Session or API key” accept either; endpoints marked “Session only” (saved searches, subscriptions) accept only the cookie, so a leaked key cannot manage credentials. “Moderator” endpoints additionally require the moderator role.

## What is not here

This reference covers every endpoint you can call. A handful are deliberately left out because calling them directly is meaningless: the Gmail and calendar consent redirects (`/me/gmail/connect`, `/me/calendar/connect`, and their callbacks), which only a browser can complete; the Telegram bot webhook; the browser-tool websocket relay; the sitemap-cursor helpers behind `/sitemap.xml`; and the `/og/*.png` social-preview cards, which render an image rather than answer with JSON.

Managing API keys (`POST`, `GET` and `DELETE` on `/me/api-keys`) is not documented here, because no API client can call it. Those endpoints accept only the browser session cookie, and additionally require a freshly proven identity — a password re-entry or a sign-in-provider check — that a script has no way to supply. Create and revoke keys in your account instead, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys); the plaintext token is shown exactly once, at creation, so store it then.

Most of this API is also a CLI. If you are writing an agent rather than an integration, `freehire` covers the same surface with less ceremony — search, tracking, the inbox and CV tailoring — over one API key.

## Original links and catalogue export

This reference covers only the endpoints the [paid API plans](https://freehire.me/jobs-api) add: job reads that carry each posting’s original links (`url`, where the application goes, and `source_url`, the original posting when it differs), and the Data plan’s full-catalogue export. `GET /data/jobs/search` and `GET /data/jobs/{slug}` take the same parameters and return the same shapes as `GET /jobs/search` and `GET /jobs/{slug}`. On every other job read, a posting with an `apply_url` (a counted freehire redirect) has `url` empty and no `source_url`; a posting without one, and an Adzuna posting (whose `url` is Adzuna’s own page), keeps `url`. Wherever the overview says to refresh a posting with `GET /jobs/{slug}`, a mirror uses `GET /data/jobs/{slug}` so it keeps the links. Send a full-access key of an API or Data plan holder as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; any other account gets `403` (the catalogue export needs the Data plan). The two `/data/jobs` endpoints are counted apart: 1,200 requests a minute on the API plan, 6,000 on the Data plan; every other endpoint, the catalogue export included, holds the 1,200-request window. The rest of the API is documented at [freehire.me/docs/api](https://freehire.me/docs/api).

## Filtering jobs



Except where noted below, these parameters apply to `GET /jobs/search` and `GET /jobs/facets`. Combine any of them with full-text `q`.



- Pass multiple values as a comma-separated list to OR them: `skills=go,rust` matches either. Repeating the param (`skills=go&skills=rust`) also works.

- Add `<param>_mode=and` to require all selected values: `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and` matches both.

- Add `<param>_exclude=<value>` to exclude matches: `company_type_exclude=outstaff` drops outstaff jobs.

- Different facets are ANDed together; numeric and boolean filters are ANDed too. The geography facets are the one exception — see below.

- Geography is a single OR group: `regions`, `countries`, `metros` and `cities` widen each other instead of narrowing. `regions=eu&countries=IT` means "in Europe **or** in Italy", so it returns everything `regions=eu` alone would. To search one country, drop the region: `countries=IT`. The four name a single concept — *where* — so picking two places reads as "either", which is what makes `regions=eu&countries=BR` ("Europe or Brazil") useful. There is no AND to switch on: `_mode=and` does not apply to geography.

- Use `regions=none` to match jobs with no resolved geography (an empty region set); it ORs with real region values and supports `_exclude` like any region.

- A param no filter reads is ignored rather than refused — so old links and saved searches keep working — and comes back in `meta.ignored_params`, with `did_you_mean` when it is only the singular of a real facet. Check it: a dropped filter otherwise looks like a genuinely broad result. At most 10 are listed per response. The same report rides on `/jobs/facets`, `/market/coverage` and `/companies`, which answer `{"data": ...}` and grow a `meta` block only when there is something to warn about. `/companies` filters on its own vocabulary, so a jobs facet sent there is reported as ignored.



### Facets



Every facet below supports repeat-OR, `_mode=and`, and `_exclude` as described above.



| Param | Filter | Values |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `collections` | Collection | yc, techstars, a16z-portfolio, a16z-speedrun, sequoia, accel, greylock, usv, bond, lightspeed, index-ventures, softbank-vision-fund, founders-fund, european, ai, mag7, bigtech, unicorn, fortune500, eastern-roots, indian-roots, ai-native, uk-skilled-worker-sponsor, nl-recognised-sponsor, us-h1b-sponsor, ca-lmia-employer, ie-permit-employer, dk-fast-track-company |

| `regions` | Region | global, north_america, latam, eu, uk, mena, africa, apac, cis, none |

| `work_mode` | Work format | remote, hybrid, onsite |

| `category` | Specialization | software_engineering, backend, frontend, fullstack, mobile, devops, sre, network_engineering, system_administration, telecommunications_engineering, it_support, data_engineering, data_science, data_analytics, ml_ai, ai_engineering, qa, security, hardware, embedded, blockchain, architecture, design, creative, engineering_design, industrial_engineering, occupational_safety, product, project_management, healthcare, skilled_trades, retail, hospitality, logistics, education, personal_services, administration, social_services, science, manufacturing, public_safety, marketing, sales, support, business_analysis, solutions_engineering, developer_relations, technical_writing, recruiting, hr, finance, legal, operations, customer_success, other. The retired value management is still accepted and answered as role_type=people_manager |

| `ai_archetype` | AI Specialization | rag_app_builder, agent_builder, cloud_ml_platform_engineer, ml_trainer_researcher, fullstack_ai_engineer, devops_infra_engineer |

| `seniority` | Seniority | intern, junior, middle, senior, lead, staff, principal, c_level |

| `role_type` | Role type | people_manager — the title names a people-management role. One value only: carrying nothing means no management marker was found, NOT that the posting is individual-contributor work, so role_type_exclude means "no marker", not "IC" |

| `skills` | Skills | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `domains` | Industry | fintech, crypto, ecommerce, gambling, gamedev, media, travel, healthcare, edtech, govtech, devtools, cybersecurity, ai, hrtech, adtech, proptech, logistics, mobility, climatetech, other |

| `company_type` | Company type | product, startup, outsource, outstaff, agency, inhouse, government |

| `countries` | Countries | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `cities` | City | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values. Recognized dictionary aliases such as München and Köln resolve to their canonical city names. |

| `metros` | Metro area | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `relocation` | Relocation | not_supported, supported, required |

| `employment_type` | Employment | full_time, part_time, contract, internship, fellowship |

| `engagement` | Contract terms | ir35_outside, ir35_inside, w2, 1099, c2c, contract_to_hire, b2b, uop, umowa_zlecenie, umowa_o_dzielo, clt, pj, tk, gph, samozanyaty, ip, freiberuflich, arbeitnehmerueberlassung, zzp, auto_entrepreneur, portage_salarial, autonomo, monotributo — employee or own business, in each market's own term (UK IR35, US W-2/1099/C2C, Polish B2B and umowy, Brazilian CLT/PJ, Russian ТК/ГПХ/самозанятость/ИП, German, Dutch, French, Spanish and Argentine freelance statuses), as the title, the description or a source's own contract-type field states it; a posting offering several carries each, one that does not say carries none. Separate from employment_type |

| `english_level` | English | none, a1, a2, b1, b2, c1, c2, native |

| `posting_language` | Job language | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `reality` | Posting reality | fresh, stale, likely-evergreen |

| `salary_currency` | Currency | USD, EUR, GBP, RUB |

| `perks` | Perks mentioned | generous_pto, four_day_week, 401k_match, parental_leave, retirement_plan, tuition_reimbursement, unlimited_pto, health_insurance, mental_health, learning_budget, home_office_stipend, sabbatical, sign_on_bonus — matched from the description; a posting without one does not mention it, which is not the same as not offering it |

| `equity` | Equity | salary_and_equity, equity_only, not_stated — not_stated means none was read, not that the job offers no equity |

| `company_slug` | Company | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `source_type` | Source type | ats, company, aggregator, social |

| `clearance_levels` | Clearance level | none, confidential, secret, top_secret, ts_sci, public_trust, interim, other. none = no detected clearance requirement (the same postings as requires_clearance=false); other = a non-US scheme (UK SC/DV, AU NV1, NATO) or a clearance stated with no level; interim is stated beside a level, not instead of one |

| `source` | Source | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `company_size` | Company size | 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1000, 1000+ |

| `education_level` | Education level | none, bachelor, master, phd |

| `salary_period` | Salary period | year, month, day, hour |

| `is_tech` | Technical role | tech, non_tech |



### Numeric & boolean filters



| Param | Filter | Values |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `visa_sponsorship` | Visa sponsorship | true, false |

| `requires_clearance` | Security clearance required | true, false |

| `via_recruiter` | Posting says a recruiter publishes it for a client | true — the description says so; false — every posting not marked, including recruiter posts that never say so |

| `former_employers` | Hiring again: companies you have worked at and left | true — signed in only, read from your experience bank; a name that does not resolve to exactly one company is left out. Anonymous, it is reported in meta.ignored_params. `/jobs/facets` never applies this filter, so its counts ignore it even for signed-in callers |

| `watchlist` | Your watchlist: companies you follow | true — signed in only; an empty watchlist matches nothing. Anonymous, it is reported in meta.ignored_params. Kept in a saved search, so `watchlist=true` is the alert for new postings at the companies you follow. `/jobs/facets` never applies this filter, so its counts ignore it |

| `new_hiring` | Just started hiring: companies that began hiring this month | true — companies with nothing open for the 90 days before the last 30 that then posted, recomputed daily (the companies `/insights/companies?sort=new` lists, without its `min_open` floor); empty until the first daily run. Not applied by alerts or by `/jobs/facets`, so its counts ignore it |

| `salary_min` | Minimum salary | integer — jobs whose minimum salary is at least this (pair with salary_currency) |

| `salary_max` | Maximum salary | integer — jobs whose maximum salary is at most this (pair with salary_currency) |

| `experience_years_min` | Minimum experience | integer — jobs requiring at least this many years |

| `experience_years_max` | Maximum experience | integer — jobs requiring at most this many years, the same figure experience_years_min bounds from below. Use 0 for jobs stating no prior experience is required. Either bound excludes jobs that state no requirement at all, unless experience_include_unspecified is set |

| `experience_include_unspecified` | Include unstated experience | true — with either experience bound, also keep the jobs that state no experience requirement (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without a bound |

| `experience_only_seniority_unspecified` | Experience only without a level | true — apply either experience bound only to the jobs that carry no seniority level; a job with a level passes the bound whatever it states. With seniority and seniority_include_unspecified this reads "one of these levels, or no level and within the bound". Has no effect without a bound |

| `seniority_include_unspecified` | Include unstated seniority | true — with seniority, also keep the jobs that carry no seniority level (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without an included seniority |

| `posted_within_days` | Posted within | integer — jobs whose SOURCE states a posting date in the last N days. Some boards restate that date on every crawl, so a job open for months can satisfy a narrow bound here; open_within_days is the one that cannot be rewritten from outside |

| `open_within_days` | Open within | integer — jobs first recorded by freehire in the last N days, i.e. how long the posting has been in the catalogue regardless of the date its source states. Independent of posted_within_days; both may be set and they narrow together |

| `apply_questions_max` | Application questions | integer ≥ 0 — jobs whose application form requires at most N questions beyond name, contact details and CV (3 = the "short form" filter). Jobs with no form freehire could read are excluded: unknown is not short |

| `auto_apply_available` | Auto-apply can attempt it | true — only postings whose ATS freehire auto-apply can currently attempt to fill and submit for; a provider-eligibility signal, never a guarantee the submission succeeds |

| `work_mode_remote_anywhere` | Remote from anywhere, other modes at home | true — with `remote` and a physical work_mode both selected and a geography facet set, reads "remote anywhere, OR hybrid/onsite within the geography" instead of ANDing them. Otherwise, or with work_mode_mode=and, it changes nothing |

| `work_mode_remote_regions` | Remote arm: regions | Region values, as regions — bound the remote arm of work_mode_remote_anywhere. Read only while it is in force |

| `work_mode_remote_countries` | Remote arm: countries | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, as countries — bound the remote arm of work_mode_remote_anywhere, ORed with work_mode_remote_regions. Read only while it is in force |



### Recipes



- **Senior Go, remote, in the CIS region** — `q=go&seniority=senior&work_mode=remote&regions=cis`

- **Backend roles, freshest first, in Germany** — `category=backend&countries=DE&sort=posted_at&order=desc`

- **One country only — no region param, or it widens back out** — `countries=IT&employment_type=contract`

- **Must use both Go and Rust** — `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and`

- **Exclude outstaff companies** — `company_type_exclude=outstaff`

- **At least $100k, with visa sponsorship** — `salary_currency=USD&salary_min=100000&visa_sponsorship=true`

- **Excluding jobs that need a security clearance** — `clearance_levels=none`

- **Jobs stating Secret or Top Secret clearance** — `clearance_levels=secret,top_secret`

- **Only jobs that need a security clearance** — `requires_clearance=true`

tags.name: Catalogue export
tags.description: Full-catalogue files for the Data plan (`api_data`). A snapshot is one gzip file, `jobs.jsonl.gz`: UTF-8 JSON Lines, one job per line, each in the same wire shape as `GET /data/jobs/{slug}` (full `description` and `url` included), covering the open, canonical, public postings the search index lists. The file is streamed, so it is not one JSON document; read it line by line. Every snapshot has a `schema_version`, a row count, a byte size and a SHA-256 to verify the download. Snapshots are named by UTC day and the last few are kept. How often a new one appears is set by the operator timer, not by this API: read `date` and `generated_at` rather than assuming a schedule. To stay current between snapshots, re-fetch single jobs with `GET /data/jobs/{slug}`. The licence is the API plan's: show the data in your own product, do not resell it as a dataset or feed, and stop showing it when the plan ends — see /terms#data-licence.

tags.name: Original job links
tags.description: Job reads for the paid API plans (`api`, `api_data`) that carry each posting's original links: `url`, where the application goes, and `source_url`, the original posting when it differs. Other job reads drop both when `apply_url`, a freehire redirect, is set; Adzuna postings keep `url`. The API plan holds its 1,200-request window here, counted apart; the Data plan's 6,000-request window applies here only (see API plans). Session or API key; any account without a paid API plan gets `403`.

get.summary: List bulk catalogue snapshots and their download links.
get.description:
Lists the finished snapshots, newest first, each with a short-lived pre-signed download URL
(about 15 minutes; call this again for a fresh link). Needs the Data plan: any other
account gets `403`. `501` means bulk files are not set up on this deployment.

get.summary: Search open jobs with their original links (API and Data plans).
get.description:
The same text query and filters as `GET /jobs/search` (the "Filtering jobs" section), with
each job's `url` (the employer's own posting) and `source_url` where it differs. The public
job reads leave both out and link only through `apply_url`. Needs a paid API plan (API or
Data): any other account gets `403`. Never cached: the answer is private to the plan holder.

get.summary: A single job with its original links (API and Data plans).
get.description:
The same answer as `GET /jobs/{slug}`, with the job's `url` and `source_url`. Needs a paid
API plan (API or Data): any other account gets `403`.

date.description: UTC day the snapshot is named by, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

schema_version.description: Version of the line shape in the file. A removed or re-meant field bumps it; a new field does not.

rows.description: Number of lines (jobs) in the file.

bytes.description: Size of the gzip file in bytes.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the gzip file, to check a download.

download_url.description: Pre-signed link to the gzip file; it works without credentials until `url_expires_at`.

CatalogueSnapshot.description: One finished bulk snapshot of the catalogue.

IgnoredParam.description:
A query param the endpoint did not read: unknown, or known but unreadable
(`min_years=lots`). Either way the answer is wider than the caller asked for.

IgnoredValues.description:
Present only when a closed-vocabulary facet (or its `_exclude` form) carried a value
outside its vocabulary — keyed by the parameter as sent, each listing the unknown values.
On a facet the value is still applied and matches no posting: alone it empties the
answer, beside other values it adds nothing to their OR, in `_exclude` it excludes
nothing. A boolean or modifier param reads it its own way (`requires_clearance=flase`
reads as true, `visa_sponsorship=yes` filters nothing), so the answer may be wider.

public_slug.description: Stable public identifier. The freehire page is https://freehire.me/jobs/{public_slug}.

url.description:
The employer's own application URL, as published. Served only by the paid API plans'
`/data/jobs` endpoints: every other job read leaves it empty wherever `apply_url` is set.
Empty too when `direct_apply` is true: that vacancy has no page elsewhere.

apply_url.description:
Where to send an applicant: a freehire redirect (`https://freehire.me/api/v1/go/{public_slug}?src=...`)
that counts the click and forwards to the employer's page. Set `src` to the surface handing the link out:
`web`, `mcp`, `ojcp`, `assistant`, `email`, `telegram` or `api`. Absent for a vacancy taking applications on freehire.

direct_apply.description:
True for a vacancy its employer published on freehire that takes applications only on
its freehire page (`https://freehire.me/jobs/{slug}`). Absent for every other posting.

location.description: The posting's own location string, verbatim and unnormalized. Filter on the geography facets instead.

source.description: Origin slug — the ATS or board this posting was crawled from.

external_id.description: The source's own identifier for the posting.

source_url.description:
The original posting when `url` points at a separately verified application
destination. Absent when both links are the same, and outside the paid API plans'
`/data/jobs` endpoints.

application_deadline.description: Source-stated last application day, inclusive. Absent when the source states no deadline.

team.description:
The department or team the posting's ATS files it under, verbatim (Greenhouse, Lever,
Ashby, Gem, Recruitee and Employment Hero state one). Absent when the source states none; not a taxonomy, so values differ
between employers.

manually_added.description: True for a hand-curated posting rather than an automated crawl.

work_mode.description: Absent when the posting's format could not be resolved.

collections.description: Curated collection slugs of the posting's company.

requires_clearance.description:
Present and `true` only when the posting states a government security-clearance
requirement. Absent otherwise — there is no `false`, because "no requirement was
detected" is not the same claim as "this posting needs no clearance".

via_recruiter.description:
Present and `true` only when the posting states that it is published by an
intermediary on a client's behalf. Absent otherwise — a recruiter who never says so is
not detected, so absence does not mean the employer posted it.

equity.description:
What the posting states about equity compensation: `salary_and_equity` (offered beside
cash pay) or `equity_only` (equity is the whole pay). Absent when the posting states
neither — "not stated", not "no equity".

clearance_levels.description:
The security-clearance levels the posting states. Present exactly when
`requires_clearance` is, absent otherwise. `other` is a non-US scheme or a clearance
stated with no level.

perks.description:
Benefits the description states it offers (see the `perks` filter for the
vocabulary). Empty when it names none of them — not a claim that the job offers none.

engagement.description:
The legal terms the posting states it engages its worker on (see the `engagement`
filter for the vocabulary). Empty when it does not say.

ai_interview_reports.description:
How many people reported that the company screens with an AI interviewer. Absent at
zero, so "no reports" is a missing field rather than a zero a badge could render.

auto_apply_available.description:
Present and `true` only when the posting's ATS provider is one freehire's auto-apply
feature can currently attempt to fill and submit for. Absent otherwise — a best-effort
provider-eligibility signal, never a guarantee of successful submission.

apply_questions.description:
How many questions the posting's application form REQUIRES beyond the standard fields
every form asks for (name, contact details, CV, cover letter), counted from the form
freehire captured from the employer's ATS. Optional questions, the equal-opportunity
survey and consent boxes are not counted. `0` means no REQUIRED question beyond the
basics. Absent when freehire holds no form for the posting — "not known", never
"long". Served by search hits and the job detail; a list read straight from the
database may omit it.

sponsored.description:
True only on a search hit placed as a paid slot (never on an organic hit). Render a
visible "Sponsored" label, and link the card to `sponsored_url`.

sponsored_url.description:
Click-tracking redirect (`/api/v1/sponsored/go/<token>`) for a sponsored hit; it always
ends at the job. `url` stays the organic link.

employment_type.description:
The employment type, the same value as `enrichment.employment_type`, lifted to the top
level. Served by `getJob` only; absent when not known.

salary.description: The pay range, the same values as `enrichment.salary_*`. Served by `getJob` only; absent when no bound is stated.

company_website.description: The employer's own site as its company record states it. Served by `getJob` only; absent when none is on record.

company_logo.description:
The employer's logo through freehire's logo proxy, resolved by the site's domain. The
proxy answers 404 when it has no mark. Served by `getJob` only, beside `company_website`.

created_at.description: When freehire first saw the posting.

last_seen_at.description: When a re-crawl last confirmed the posting was still live.

closed_at.description: Non-null once the posting is no longer open. Only `getJob` ever serves such a row.

enrichment_version.description: Bumped when the enrichment contract changes — use it to detect re-enriched rows.

my_vote.description: The calling user's vote; 0 or null without a signed-in caller.

referral_available.description:
True when the company has an approved employee referrer. Served by `getJob` only;
absent on every list and search row.

recruiter_contacts_available.description:
True when a recruiter-contact lookup can run for the posting: the feature is configured
and the company has a website on record. Served by `getJob` only.

auto_apply_status.description:
The caller's own auto-apply status for the posting: `queued` (live, undecided),
`failed` (given up: dead-lettered, or parked for missing form data) or `declined`
(the candidate's permanent decision). Served by `getJob` to a signed-in caller with
an attempt; absent for everyone else.

Job.description:
One posting, as every job endpoint serves it. TestJobSchemaCoversWireShape
(internal/job/jobview) fails when jobview.Job serves a key this model lacks.

summary.description: The one synthesized field — a 1-2 sentence synopsis, always present on an enriched posting.

requirements.description:
Requirements the posting states (at most 30, each at most 200 characters): the
model's list, or the deterministic extractor's when the model has not reached the
posting. `priority` is `required` or `preferred`.

JobEnrichment.description:
Model-extracted attributes, every field omitted when the posting did not state it.
`work_mode`, `regions`, `countries`, `cities` and `skills` are deliberately NOT here —
those are served top-level from the deterministic dictionaries, and the model's own
values for them are not published.

level.description: How strongly the evidence reads, e.g. `possible`.

criteria_total.description: How many criteria exist, so `criteria` reads as N-of-total.

contributors.description: Number of independent user reports, once past the disclosure gate.

ats_checked_at.description: When the posting was last looked for on the employer's own ATS. Present only when the `ats_absent` criterion fired.

JobGhost.description:
Hedged "is anyone actually hiring for this" verdict, raised only when evidence fires —
most postings carry none, so an absent value means "no signal", never "verified real".
Attached by `searchJobs`, `getJob` and the plain jobs list. NOT attached by
`agentSearchJobs` or `getSimilarJobs`, so its absence on those two is not evidence
either way.

repost_count.description: How many times this role has been reposted.

mass_posting_count.description: How many near-identical postings the same role cluster holds.

fake_freshness.description: True when the stated posting date looks refreshed rather than real.

JobReality.description: Signals about whether the posting reflects a real, current opening.

JobSalary.description: A posting's pay range: either bound may be absent, never both.

ignored_params.description: Absent when every param was read.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` counts only what was read, not the whole match.

Problem.description:
Every refusal, whatever its status: `{"error": msg}`. `code` is set only where a
client branches on the reason (the auth flows).

CookieSession.name: hire_token
CookieSession.description: Browser session cookie set on sign-in (HttpOnly, same-origin).

PersonalApiKey.description: Personal API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
